summary: This benchmark evaluates cross-model activation transplants from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B into Qwen2.5-32B, comparing uncalibrated edit magnitudes against fitted magnitude scaling and norm-matched random controls. While omitting magnitude calibration substantially reduces reversal rates from 81.66% to 18.15%, the raw interface maintains a statistically significant advantage over random directions. The methodology is well-controlled with paired intervals and ablation baselines, though the presentation is extremely concise and depends heavily on external repository references for mathematical formulation.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design featuring paired comparisons across an identical 507-pair cohort, backed by exact confidence intervals.
Effective use of a norm-matched random orthogonal control (0/507 reversals) confirming that the uncalibrated interface direction conveys non-trivial semantic signal.
Hardware environment, execution time (2m 38s), and exact verification entry points (`uv run`) are clearly specified.
weaknesses: The 470-word text is excessively compressed, omitting formal mathematical definitions of the 7-coordinate affine interface and basis projection.
Evaluation is confined strictly to a single synthetic arithmetic digit-completion task, leaving generalizability across broader language tasks unverified.
No official supporting code repository was formally submitted with the review package, relegating verification to text and raw external links.
suggestions: Incorporate the mathematical formulation and projection equations of the 14B affine interface directly into the text rather than relying on external commit references.
Expand evaluation to multi-digit arithmetic or general reasoning benchmarks to quantify off-target degradation caused by uncalibrated interventions.
Formally bundle reproduction scripts and environment lockfiles in a published supporting repository.
